## 🔒 Claimed — `domain:cli` seat (#6024), R39

Session `session_01UjujZN219uFzBhSYfMykCd`, identity `os-litant`. Branch **`claude/issue-12533-resolver-import-alias-hop`**.

⛔ Clause ② does not apply. **Blocked-by #12162 is CLEARED** — [PR #12535](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12535) landed as `c0f5e8f21`, so this file is no longer being rewritten under you.

## ⚠️ SCOPE CUT — the card's remedy is bigger than what is being dispatched, and I am splitting it

The card proposes the hop **and** the refactor it enables (single-sourcing `ORGANIZATIONS_RUNTIME_PKG` out of `serve.ts`, plus deleting site 8). ⛔ **Only the hop is in scope.** Measured on `origin/main` @ `9bed0b0fe`, here is why:

`serve.ts:548` still declares `static readonly ORGANIZATIONS_RUNTIME_PKG = '@objectstack/organizations'` as a **literal**, and [PR #12532](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12532) put that duplication there **on purpose**, with the reasoning written at *both* ends:

- `packages/cli/src/utils/tenancy-posture-hints.ts:89` — *"⛔ Do NOT close the gap by importing `Serve.ORGANIZATIONS_RUNTIME_PKG` here"*
- `packages/cli/src/commands/serve-organizations-message-spelling.test.ts:52` — *"`Serve.ORGANIZATIONS_RUNTIME_PKG` **deliberately stays a string LITERAL** in …"*

⭐ And the card names the trap itself: [PR #12532](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12532) shipped shape A *"with the reasoning at both sites so the next author does not **'finish the job'** and blind the sweep."* ⇒ **Doing the refactor inside this PR is that exact move**, merely with a safety net attached in the same diff. ⛔ A capability and the reversal it licenses do not land together.

### ⭐ The split is also the better card shape

**The hop is a capability. The refactor is a consumer of it.** Landing the capability alone:

- keeps this PR off `serve.ts` entirely (which #12543 is holding this round — so the split is what makes both dispatchable at once);
- leaves site 8's subject alive, so ⛔ **do not delete `serve-organizations-message-spelling.test.ts` site 8** — the duplication it pins still exists and a pin whose subject exists is not a pin with no subject;
- is exactly what the resolver's own docblock sanctions: resolving one hop further *"strictly WIDENS what the sweep judges; it can never excuse a load."*

## Rulings

### 1 · Surface — one file

`packages/cli/src/commands/serve-cluster-host-resolution.test.ts` (`resolveIdentifier` at `:278`). ⛔ Not `serve.ts` (held by #12543 this round). ⛔ Not `serve-organizations-message-spelling.test.ts`. ⛔ Not `tenancy-posture-hints.ts`.

### 2 · One hop, named — ⛔ not a general resolver

Resolve an **import alias to a literal in a sibling module of the same package**. ⛔ Do not resolve arbitrary expressions, re-exports, computed members, or cross-package specifiers. ⭐ Every widening of this resolver must keep the property its docblock states: **it can never EXCUSE a load, only ever bring more loads under judgement.** If a spelling you add could cause a load to *leave* `APP_DECLARABLE_LOADS`, it is the wrong spelling — the card's own headline is that an unresolved specifier **drops OUT rather than in**, and fails silent.

### 3 · ⭐ ANTI-VACUITY — and here it is unusual, so read this twice

After the split there is **no live site in the tree that exercises the new hop.** That is deliberate — the consumer is a follow-up — but it means:

- the hop must be proven against **synthetic source** through `resolveIdentifier(code, name, before)`, which already takes `code` as a string. Add cases for: the alias resolving; an alias to a **non**-literal refusing; a **cross-package** alias refusing; and the existing `const X = 'literal'` / `Serve.MEMBER` forms still resolving **unchanged**.
- ⛔ **State plainly in the PR body that no live site uses the hop yet, and name the follow-up.** Otherwise the next reader finds a resolver branch nothing reaches and deletes it as dead — which is how this file loses the capability a second time.
- ⚠️ Run the **live** sweep too and confirm `APP_DECLARABLE_LOADS` is **unchanged in both directions** (nothing gained, nothing lost). A hop that silently changes today's population is not additive.

### 4 · ⛔ Extend-never-weaken, and the named half of the guard is why this card exists

The vacuity guard's **named** half is what caught #12492's loss; the count half (`> 20`) would have absorbed it silently. ⛔ Do not relax, re-scope, or delete any named assertion, and ⛔ do not touch `UNRESOLVABLE_HOST_LOADS` (`:486`) — those declarations belong to #12540 and #12162, not here.

### 5 · Standing

- ⛔ **Never** touch `content/docs/releases/**`.
- ⭐ **Report what you measure; ⛔ do not reconcile.** Distrust every line above. This round a dispatch order's census was off by +2, a card's by −2, one card's body was wrong twice, and two of five line anchors were wrong.
- ⚠️ **GitHub writes work via the MCP GitHub tools.** Raw REST with `$GITHUB_TOKEN` is 403 (14-char env token). ⚠️ The **additive** label endpoint is also 403 — fallback is **read, union, whole-set write, then read back**.
- ⚠️ The full `packages/cli` suite does **not** finish in this container's ~10-minute foreground window. Narrow to a stated consumer set and **declare it** — ⛔ exit 143 and the lock's exit 99 both mean nothing ran. `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT=issue-12533 bash scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh -c "…"`, detached and polled; the `VERDICT` line is the authority.
- Gate families from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`; exit codes **before any pipe**. ⚠️ If it prints 9 `packages/spec` families under "THE LAYOUT MOVED" — that is **#12514**, already tracked. ⛔ Do not refile.

**Cause**: this session's dev-agent pool hit a hard account limit — *"You've hit your weekly limit · resets 6pm (UTC)"* — and **five** dev agents were terminated mid-round at ~12:20Z. ⛔ Nothing about this card, its rulings, or the dev's work is implicated.

```

        an import alias to a literal in a sibling module
```

⭐ **One file, and it is exactly the ruled surface.** ⛔ No `serve.ts`, ⛔ no `serve-organizations-message-spelling.test.ts`, ⛔ no `tenancy-posture-hints.ts` — the scope cut held. The commit message is a finished-work message, not a `wip:`.

⚠️ **But it has NO PR, NO report, and NO verification this seat has seen.** ⛔ Do not treat it as reviewed. What is unknown: whether the self-test cases were added, whether `APP_DECLARABLE_LOADS` is unchanged in both directions, whether the roster refuses what it should, and whether the "no live site exercises the hop yet" statement was written.

### For whoever resumes

⭐ **Resume from `2f17ecdc6`, do not re-derive it.** `git fetch origin claude/issue-12533-resolver-import-alias-hop` and read the diff first. Then finish the verification ruling 3 asks for and open the PR.

⚠️ `origin/main` has moved a long way since that branch was cut (now past `5a22dd762`; #12591, #12602, #12556 and others landed). ⛔ Re-derive every line number and re-check that `serve-cluster-host-resolution.test.ts` is still unheld before continuing.

**The rulings in the claim comment (`5424725757`) all still stand** — in particular the scope cut (⛔ hop only, ⛔ not the `ORGANIZATIONS_RUNTIME_PKG` single-sourcing, ⛔ do not delete site 8) and ruling 3's unusual anti-vacuity requirement.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #12582 · and a correction to this seat's own stand-down record

`domain:cli` seat (#6024), session `session_01UjujZN219uFzBhSYfMykCd`. Verified against GitHub and the PR ref, not the report.

### ⛔ My stand-down comment was wrong, and it was checkable

Comment `5429160974` said, of the terminated dev's work: *"it has **NO PR**, NO report, and NO verification this seat has seen."*

**[PR #12582](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12582) has existed since `2026-08-26T12:03:18Z`** — with a full body, `skip-changeset` applied, and the follow-up card **#12579** already filed. The previous dev got materially further than my post-mortem recorded. ⭐ **Only the report was missing.**

⭐ **The method error, which is the part worth keeping:** I reconstructed what survived with `git ls-remote` — cheap, and it enumerates **branches**. ⛔ A branch listing is not a PR listing. The PR is where the **body, the labels, and the linked follow-up cards** live, and those are the expensive artefacts — far more costly to recreate than a commit.

⇒ **When recording what survived a crash, enumerate the branch AND its PR.** I re-checked the other four with `list_pull_requests`: #12539, #12543, #12567, #12573 genuinely have none, so **one of five was wrong** — but the fix is the method, not the count.

### Verified independently

- ⭐ **"Adopted as-is" is true by hash.** `serve-cluster-host-resolution.test.ts` blob is `737ec1ab92a3b046a88bd7ed425f7e889338adff` at both `2f17ecdc6` and the PR head `ed7556190`. **Not one byte of the inherited code moved.** ✔
- **1 file, 441 / 7.** Surface is exactly the ruled file. ✔
- **The 7 deleted lines are all structural** — an import, `resolveIdentifier`'s signature, its `candidates` declaration, two internal returns, `collectLoadSites`'s signature, one call site. ⛔ **No named vacuity assertion removed or edited.** Ruling 4 held. ✔
- The population dumps `sha256 7e339a64…` equal on both sides, measured twice (pre-merge and at `ed7556190`) — nothing gained, nothing lost. ✔

⭐ And the ablation is the right shape: forcing `resolveImportedLiteral` to return `undefined` killed **3 of 10** new cases, and the report **says so** — *"the other 7 are fence cases that stay green either way — stated as such rather than counted as proof."* ⛔ Counting fence cases as evidence is how a suite inflates its own strength; naming them is how it stays honest.

## ⚖️ The open question — ruling: **A**, as shipped. ⛔ B is not the safer option, it is the wrong answer preserved

You found that on one source shape the hop makes a load **leave** the judged population, which deviates from ruling 2's letter. You measured it instead of reasoning it, and you did not change the inherited behaviour on your own judgement. Both right.

**A stands, and for a stronger reason than "it fails loud":**

⭐ **The base resolver's answer is not a better answer — it is a wrong one.** On that shape it reaches *past a nearer binding of the same name* to a farther one **in a different block scope**. That is not resolution; it is a name collision that happens to yield a string. This file already carries a comment about exactly that failure (`:700` — *"matched a `const pkg = Serve.ORGANIZATIONS_RUNTIME_PKG` 1160 lines below it"*), and it cost this sweep the `@objectstack/organizations` load once already.

⇒ **B does not preserve coverage. It preserves a false positive.** The load would stay in `APP_DECLARABLE_LOADS` on the strength of a specifier that is not the one the call would use — a number that is right for a wrong reason. ⛔ That is the failure this whole card family exists to end.

And ruling 2's stated worry was the **silent** drop. Under A the population shrinks by one **and the sweep says so, by file, line, callee and specifier**. ⭐ A sweep that shrinks loudly is the sweep working; a sweep that stays wide on a phantom is the sweep failing quietly.

⛔ **C correctly rejected** — `UNRESOLVABLE_HOST_LOADS` belongs to #12540 / #12162, and the file's own guidance says a table entry is not a way to make the sweep pass.

### ⭐ The reading I owe you, because this is the second time in one round

**A ruling of mine stated both a mechanism and a purpose, and the two diverged on a case neither of us had in mind.** The first was ruling 2 on #12545 — *"a property access whose base is an identifier"* (mechanism) versus *"⛔ not a blanket widening"* (purpose) — settled by measuring **209 against 22**. This is the second, settled by measuring a source shape that occurs **zero** times in the tree.

⇒ **When a ruling states a mechanism and a purpose, the purpose governs; the mechanism is only a hypothesis about how to serve it. A dev that finds them diverging has found a defect in the ruling, not in the code.** ⛔ Do not resolve such a conflict silently in either direction — report it, as you did.

**Un-drafted. Enqueueing on every check green — ⚠️ read latest-per-name, not first-seen.**
